marked_text:
Lina Vatu, berth clerk on the late shift, scratched this on the back of a damp docket while the launch Mako waited in [[place]]Port Vila[[/]]. A shaft bush has to be priced before dawn and the chand lers will not agree. She caught the shouts in the order they crossed the wharf:
[[comp]]860[[/]]
[[comp]]415[[/]]
[[comp]]290[[/]]
[[comp]]640[[/]]
[[comp]]510[[/]]
[[comp]]735[[/]]
[[comp]]380[[/]]
[[comp]]955[[/]]
STAMP: CANCELLED slip PV-188, the old quote of 700 was ruled out in red pencil. Under it she wrote "plis sevem kopi" and the crease split the word bush-
ing so the tail sits on the next line. Diesel on the corner, no signature, carbon faint.

ask.name: place
ask.instruction: Town written on the damp docket

ask.name: figure
ask.instruction: Harbour price halfway between the two middle quotes

marked_text:
Morning at the Monte Cafe shed, [[place]]Sao Tome[[/]]. Paulo Mendes, cocoa grader, weighed the wet sacks before the fer-
ry horn and kept only the second look at the jumping scale: [[comp]]320[[/]], [[comp]]80[[/]], [[comp]]250[[/]], [[comp]]150[[/]]. A drawer card still says 275 and he will not reuse it. He muttered "nota de hoje, sem falta" while the photo OCR split "grad er". STAMP: AG-19, purple, half off the page, coffee ring through the corner, no second initial.

ask.name: figure
ask.instruction: Sack weight halfway between the two central readings

marked_text:
Ruth Warren, radio operator, copied spare-bin counts for the cliff shed at [[place]]Adamstown[[/]] on [[logged]]9 April 2026[[/]]. Six bins, counted by tor ch because the genera-
tor coughed: [[comp]]160[[/]] [[comp]]40[[/]] [[comp]]210[[/]] [[comp]]90[[/]] [[comp]]70[[/]] [[comp]]180[[/]]. A faded chit underneath still reads bin total 150, which she refuses. Margin note "copie recue". STAMP: PITC-04, purple, half off the edge, carbon smeared, no countersign.

ask.instruction: Day the bins were counted by torch

ask.name: figure
ask.instruction: Spare count halfway between the two middle bins

ing across the crease. No skipper signature, salt on the margin.

Rain on the awnings, and Omar Willems, market inspector, walked the morning stalls in [[place]]Philipsburg[[/]]. He logged one crate count each visit and folded the last pair under the carbon. "Graag bevestigen" sits on the Dutch line he never translates. The mar ket sheet reads:
[[obs]]2026-04-03|33[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-04-07|37[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-04-12|44[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-04-16|49[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-04-21|56[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-04-27|68[[/]]
STAMP: clipboard tag PB-29 claimed 81 crates and he marked it wrong. A staple hole breaks inspec-
tor in half. Pencil smear, no second initial, awning drip on the corner.

ask.instruction: Stall counts on the folded carbon

marked_text:
Shutter up, kettle not yet boiled. Celia Brooks, clinic runner at the morning window in [[place]]Saint John's[[/]], writes how many people were still outside. She muttered "likkle line long" and locked three later mornings in the tin. The clin ic slate shows:
[[obs]]2026-05-02|28[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-05-04|36[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-05-07|43[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-05-11|51[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-05-15|62[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-05-19|74[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-05-24|89[[/]]
STAMP: yesterday board SJ-3 said 95 and the nurse struck it. The hole punch tears shutt-
er across the middle. Blue ink, no stamp date, a thumbprint on the lower corner.
